sector: A seed-stage software company selling scheduling infrastructure to logistics operations teams, with a main product and two sub-products.
founded_place_size: Founded 2024, Denver, Colorado. Eleven people, six weeks out from their first developer conference.
about: Halcyon Grid builds scheduling infrastructure for logistics operations teams, sold by the seat to the engineers and operations leads who run the floor. The product is judged on reliability, and the brand is meant to say the same thing the software does: precise, plain, and built to be depended on.
audience: Engineering and operations leads at mid-sized logistics firms, decided by a technical evaluator rather than a brand buyer. An audience that reads fuss as sloppiness and crispness as competence.
price_positioning: Seats 20 to 60 dollars per user per month. Mid-market infrastructure pricing, sold on reliability and evaluation rather than on brand aspiration. The visual language reads as engineering credibility, never as marketing spend.

palette.name: Grid Indigo
palette.role: mandatory as the main mark colour in the three logo SVGs
palette.usage: The main flat colour of every mark in the three logo SVGs and of every full-colour mark elsewhere, taken from the indigo end of the gradient in halcyon_master_mark.png, halcyon_sub_mark_dispatch.png and halcyon_sub_mark_relay.png; also the ground of a reversed example.

palette.name: Signal Violet
palette.usage: An optional second flat colour inside a mark, from the violet end of the same gradient, and thin rules or dividers, as the rule beside the portrait on exhibitor_card_2025_PRINT.pdf. Never a ground, a panel or type.

palette.name: Slate Ink
palette.role: mandatory wherever type sits on Paper White
palette.usage: The HALCYON / GRID wordmark, the signature move's dense black brick, and every heading, body line, label and caption on Paper White, as all the type on exhibitor_card_2025_PRINT.pdf; also a one-colour version of a mark on a light ground outside the logo SVGs, and the ground of a reversed example.

palette.name: Cool Steel
palette.usage: Clear-space guides, dimension lines and hairline rules. Never a mark colour, a ground, a panel or type.

palette.name: Paper White
palette.role: mandatory as the page ground of the usage guide and the team page
palette.usage: The page ground, as on exhibitor_card_2025_PRINT.pdf, and all type and marks reversed out of Grid Indigo or Slate Ink. Never a ground in the three logo SVGs, which stay transparent.

typography: Halcyon Grid sets three families it already owns, and it inverts the usual scale on purpose. Step 01 is the wordmark in Gotham Ultra, caps stacked flush left on two lines at 40 px with leading at 23 px, that being 0.82 of the 28 px cap height, tracking at 0 units and never letterspaced, held at a ceiling of 40 px on screen or 12 pt in print so weight rather than scale carries it. Step 02 is the screen headline in Inter Regular at 64 px on 68 px with tracking at -10 units, larger than the wordmark in size and beneath it in hierarchy, with print documentation headings at 18 pt on 24 pt and product names at 20 px on 26 px. Step 03 is interface and documentation copy in Inter Regular at 10 pt on 14 pt, tracking 0 units, always tabular figures, measure held to a maximum of 65 characters, with grid references in JetBrains Mono Regular at the same size. Step 04 is captions in Inter Regular at 8 pt on 11 pt with tracking at +8 units. Gotham Ultra is the wordmark and nothing else.
voice: Direct, unadorned, engineer to engineer. No hype, no gloss. Example line: "Sharp, plain, restrained. If something in our own list turns out to be a bad idea, tell us before you build it."
brand_assets_status: The three marks (the main mark and two sub-product marks) were generated by the founder in an AI tool two years ago, on separate nights with different settings. Only the soft-edged raster exports survive, with no source files. They go soft as soon as anyone scales them, and the printer and the app store listing have both said they cannot use them. No production vector artwork exists.
values: Reliability and restraint. Geometry over decoration, documentation over marketing. Say honestly what the artwork can and cannot do, including the founder's gradient.

scale.note: The wordmark block, and the only display setting in the system. The slash in the sample marks the stack: caps flush left on two lines, leading at 0.82 of the 28 px cap height, which is 23 px, so both words lock into one dense brick. 40 px is the ceiling on screen and 12 pt in print. Deliberate inversion: this block sits above step 02 in hierarchy and below it in size, because weight rather than scale carries it.

The screen headline, and the largest type in the system. The existing prose assigns every heading to Inter and reserves Gotham Ultra for the wordmark alone, so the text face carries this step. Print documentation headings set at 18 pt on 24 pt, product names at 20 px on 26 px.

scale.sample: Precise, plain, and built to be depended on.
scale.note: Interface and documentation copy, always with tabular figures so numbers stay in column. Both numbers already stated in the existing prose. Grid references themselves set in JetBrains Mono Regular at the same size and leading.

scale.sample: Seats 20 to 60 dollars per user per month.
scale.note: Captions and footnotes. 8 pt comes from the existing prose; leading and the slight positive tracking are added so small copy holds on Paper White.

type_system.signature_move: The wordmark is Gotham Ultra caps stacked flush left on two lines with leading at 0.82 of cap height, 23 px at a 40 px setting, held deliberately small so it reads as one dense black brick rather than a large logo. Step 01 carries the brick, and tabular figures at step 03 keep the engineering half of the house behaviour visible.
rules: Never letterspace the Ultra. Tracking on the wordmark stays at 0 units.
The wordmark never goes above 40 px on screen or 12 pt in print. Weight rather than scale carries it.
The wordmark is always caps stacked flush left on two lines with leading at 0.82 of cap height, so both words lock into one block.
Gotham Ultra is the wordmark only. No heading, subheading or body line is ever set in it.
Interface and documentation figures are always tabular so columns align.
Grid references are always JetBrains Mono Regular, never Inter.
No hype and no gloss in the copy that fills the scale. Direct, engineer to engineer.

palette_rules.distribution: Grounds and panels are Paper White; Grid Indigo or Slate Ink may be the ground only of a reversed example. On Paper White all type is Slate Ink, as all type on exhibitor_card_2025_PRINT.pdf is, and so is the wordmark, the signature move's dense black brick. In the three transparent logo SVGs every mark is Grid Indigo, with Signal Violet as its only possible second colour, and the wordmark and any product name are Slate Ink. On any other light ground a mark takes the same colours or is a one-colour Slate Ink version. On Grid Indigo or Slate Ink, marks and type are Paper White. Outside the marks, Signal Violet and Cool Steel are for rules, dividers and clear-space guides only, together no more than 5% of the designed, non-photographic area, never a ground, a panel or type.
palette_rules.opacity: Every palette colour is used solid, at 100% opacity. No tint, transparency, gradient, shadow, blur or blend mode is applied to any palette colour, and no scrim, gradient or overlay of any colour, black and white included, is laid over a photograph.
palette_rules.forbidden: No glow, halo, gradient, drop shadow, bevel, gloss highlight or metallic effect on any mark, type, panel, rule or icon, and no colour outside the five palette hexes (#2B2E6B, #6C4BD8, #1C2230, #8A93A6 and #F6F7FA) for marks, type, panels, rules or icons.
palette_rules.photography: The eleven portraits keep their own photographic colour and are never tinted, duotoned or overlaid toward Grid Indigo or Signal Violet. Any colour correction moves a portrait toward neutral, never toward a palette colour, including the warm lamp cast of team_kraft.jpg and the slight green cast of team_whitfield.jpg.
